name: The Wu
description: Childan is making up a legendary story and trying to sell his forgery — a necklace with a strong sense of " Wu " to the Kasouras. But Mr. Kasoura is challenging the truth of Childan's story. So he is going to ask a few questions about Childan's so-called "personal treasure" necklace. This "personal treasure" is a multiset $$$S$$$ of $$$m$$$ " 01-strings ". A " 01-string " is a string that contains $$$n$$$ characters " 0 " and " 1 ". For example, if $$$n=4$$$, strings " 0110 ", " 0000 ", and " 1110 " are " 01-strings ", but " 00110 " (there are $$$5$$$ characters, not $$$4$$$) and " zero " (unallowed characters) are not. Note that the multiset $$$S$$$ can contain equal elements. Frequently, Mr. Kasoura will provide a " 01-string " $$$t$$$ and ask Childan how many strings $$$s$$$ are in the multiset $$$S$$$ such that the " Wu " value of the pair $$$(s, t)$$$ is not greater than $$$k$$$. Mrs. Kasoura and Mr. Kasoura think that if $$$s_i = t_i$$$ ($$$1\leq i\leq n$$$) then the " Wu " value of the character pair equals to $$$w_i$$$, otherwise $$$0$$$. The " Wu " value of the " 01-string " pair is the sum of the " Wu " values of every character pair. Note that the length of every " 01-string " is equal to $$$n$$$. For example, if $$$w=[4, 5, 3, 6]$$$, " Wu " of (" 1001 ", " 1100 ") is $$$7$$$ because these strings have equal characters only on the first and third positions, so $$$w_1+w_3=4+3=7$$$. You need to help Childan to answer Mr. Kasoura's queries. That is to find the number of strings in the multiset $$$S$$$ such that the " Wu " value of the pair is not greater than $$$k$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$q$$$ ($$$1\leq n\leq 12$$$, $$$1\leq q, m\leq 5\cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the " 01-strings ", the size of the multiset $$$S$$$, and the number of queries. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_n$$$ ($$$0 \le w_i \le 100$$$) — the value of the $$$i$$$-th caracter. Each of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains the " 01-string " $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$ — the string in the multiset $$$S$$$. Each of the next $$$q$$$ lines contains the " 01-string " $$$t$$$ of length $$$n$$$ and integer $$$k$$$ ($$$0\leq k\leq 100$$$) — the query.
output_specification: For each query, print the answer for this query.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1017D — The Wu [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
